candidates.text:
Standard: 1.T.C.1
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Writing, Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Explain how authors use language to achieve a specific purpose and address a target audience, and create texts in various modes.
Skills:
- Identify the general purpose of a variety of texts.
- Identify the target audience of a variety of texts.
- Identify different modes of communication: print, digital, auditory, and visual.
- Create texts in teacher-selected modes such as print, digital, auditory, and/or visual.
Observable behaviors:
- Identify the general purpose of a text, such as telling stories, providing information, sharing opinions, or explaining ideas.
- Recognize the target audience for different texts.
- Identify different modes of communication including print, digital, auditory, and visual.
- Create texts using teacher-selected modes such as print, digital, auditory, or visual formats.
Pedagogy terms: purpose, audience, modes of communication, text creation
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify the general purpose and target audience in various texts and recognize different modes of communication.
- written_production: Create texts in teacher-selected modes such as print or digital.
- representation_modeling: Create texts in teacher-selected modes including auditory and visual formats.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how authors use language for a specific purpose and target audience.
Codes: 1.T.C.1
candidates.label: Purpose & Audience

candidates.text:
Standard: 1.P.EICC.2.d
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Writing, Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK3_strategic_thinking
Competency: Interpret and create texts to help analyze and evaluate texts and ideas.
Skills:
- Interpret texts to analyze ideas.
- Construct texts to evaluate ideas.
Observable behaviors:
- Explain the meaning of texts in their own words.
- Create texts that express their understanding of ideas.
- Use texts to compare and think critically about ideas.
Pedagogy terms: interpretation, text construction, analysis, evaluation, ideas, author and audience
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify ideas and information in texts to support analysis and evaluation.
- oral_production: Explain interpretations and evaluations of texts orally.
- written_production: Create written texts that express analysis and evaluation of ideas.
- procedural_application: Use texts intentionally to analyze and evaluate ideas.
- representation_modeling: Construct texts that represent understanding of ideas.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain reasoning behind interpretations and evaluations of texts.
- comprehension_response: Respond to texts by interpreting and evaluating ideas.
Codes: 1.P.EICC.2.d

Standard: 1.P.EICC.3.d
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Summarize parts of a text and create visual representations to help understand what is read.
Skills:
- Summarize sections of the text to maintain understanding.
- Visualize sections of the text to maintain understanding.
Observable behaviors:
- Retell key points from sections of a text in their own words.
- Draw or create pictures that represent important ideas from the text.
- Use summaries and visuals to check understanding while reading.
Pedagogy terms: summarize, visualize, comprehension strategies, meaning-making
Required student actions:
- oral_production: Summarize sections of a text orally to show understanding.
- written_production: Create drawings or visual representations of text sections to support comprehension.
- procedural_application: Use summarizing and visualizing strategies during reading to maintain understanding.
- representation_modeling: Model summarizing and visualizing parts of a text to maintain comprehension.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how summarizing and visualizing help maintain understanding of the text.
- comprehension_response: Summarize and visualize sections of the text to demonstrate ongoing comprehension.
Codes: 1.P.EICC.3.d

Standard: 1.T.RA.2
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Use parts of texts to support ideas or answers and explore different sources of information to make connections on various topics.
Skills:
- Refer to parts of texts when supporting an idea, answer, or opinion.
- Explore various sources of information, including print, digital, and personal communication.
Observable behaviors:
- Point to or name parts of a text when explaining an idea or answer.
- Identify and use information from print, digital, and personal communication sources.
- Discuss connections made from exploring multiple sources on a topic.
Pedagogy terms: text evidence, sources, information exploration, connections
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify parts of texts that support ideas or answers.
- oral_production: Explain ideas or answers using parts of texts and discuss information from various sources.
- procedural_application: Use parts of texts to support ideas or answers and explore various sources of information.
- investigation_handson: Explore various sources of information including print, digital, and personal communication.
- reasoning_explanation: Refer to parts of texts to support ideas or answers and explain connections made from multiple sources.
- comprehension_response: Use text parts to address specific questions and integrate information from various sources to understand topics.
Codes: 1.T.RA.2
candidates.label: Curating Sources & Evidence

candidates.text:
Standard: 1.T.T.2.a
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Writing
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Identify techniques used to create expository texts, including recognizing the main topic and supporting details.
Skills:
- Identify the main topic in an expository text.
- Identify supporting details in an expository text.
- Recognize techniques used to craft expository texts.
Observable behaviors:
- Point out the main topic in an expository text.
- Identify supporting details that explain or describe the main topic.
- Recognize techniques authors use to organize and present information in expository texts.
Pedagogy terms: expository text, main topic, supporting details, text features, text structure
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify the main topic and supporting details in expository texts.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how supporting details relate to the main topic in an expository text.
- comprehension_response: Describe the main topic and supporting details when reading expository texts.
Codes: 1.T.T.2.a

Standard: 1.P.EICC.3
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Vocabulary
Cognitive demand: DOK3_strategic_thinking
Competency: Students engage with complex texts for different purposes by using comprehension strategies before, during, and after reading to understand and make meaning.
Skills:
- Establish a purpose and set goals for reading
- Monitor comprehension and adjust strategies as needed
- Scan and skim the text to note useful structures and sections
- Draw from and integrate prior knowledge with the text, addressing inconsistencies or gaps
- Summarize and visualize sections of the text to maintain understanding
- Make and track predictions about upcoming events and information
- Make, track, and support inferences about different levels of meaning
- Determine meanings of unfamiliar words and concepts using context, academic vocabulary, and word parts
Observable behaviors:
- Set a purpose and goals for reading a text
- Monitor understanding while reading and adjust strategies as needed
- Scan and skim texts to identify useful structures and sections
- Connect prior knowledge to new information in the text and resolve inconsistencies
- Summarize and create mental images of text sections to maintain understanding
- Make and track predictions about upcoming events or information in the text
- Make, track, and support inferences about meanings within the text
- Determine meanings of unfamiliar words using context, academic vocabulary, and word parts
Pedagogy terms: comprehension strategies, monitor comprehension, set reading goals, scan and skim, prior knowledge, summarize, visualize, predict, infer, context clues, academic vocabulary, word parts
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify text structures and unfamiliar words using context and word parts
- procedural_application: Apply comprehension strategies such as setting goals, monitoring understanding, scanning, summarizing, predicting, and inferring while reading
- representation_modeling: Visualize and summarize sections of text to support understanding
- reasoning_explanation: Explain inferences and predictions about text meaning and events
- comprehension_response: Summarize text sections and track comprehension progress
Codes: 1.P.EICC.3
candidates.label: Comprehension Strategies

candidates.text:
Standard: 1.T.T.2
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Writing
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Identify and use expository techniques to understand and create texts that explain a topic with facts and details.
Skills:
- Identify techniques used to craft expository texts, including main topic and supporting details.
- Describe the connection between two individuals, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text.
- Use knowledge of expository techniques to introduce a topic, supply facts about the topic, and provide a sense of closure.
Observable behaviors:
- Point out the main topic and supporting details in an expository text.
- Explain how two people, events, ideas, or pieces of information in a text are connected.
- Write a short text that introduces a topic, includes facts about it, and ends with a closing sentence.
Pedagogy terms: expository text, main topic, supporting details, text connections, introduce topic, facts, closure
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify main topic and supporting details in expository texts.
- oral_production: Describe connections between individuals, events, ideas, or information in a text.
- written_production: Write an expository text that introduces a topic, provides facts, and includes a sense of closure.
- procedural_application: Use knowledge of expository techniques to organize and write about a topic.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how two elements in a text are connected.
Codes: 1.T.T.2
candidates.label: Expository Techniques

candidates.text:
Standard: 1.P.ST.2.b
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Writing
Cognitive demand: DOK3_strategic_thinking
Competency: Use what you know about the author, audience, and context to identify and express a clear point of view or unique perspective when reading or creating texts.
Skills:
- Draw from knowledge of the author to understand texts.
- Draw from knowledge of the audience to understand texts.
- Draw from knowledge of the context to understand texts.
- Use this knowledge to discern a clear point of view or unique perspective when interpreting texts.
- Use this knowledge to establish a clear point of view or unique perspective when constructing texts.
Observable behaviors:
- Explain who the author is writing for and why.
- Identify the context of a text and how it influences the message.
- State a clear point of view or perspective about a text.
- Create a text that shows a unique perspective based on understanding the author, audience, and context.
Pedagogy terms: author, audience, context, point of view, perspective, interpret, construct
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Recognize the author, audience, and context in texts.
- oral_production: Express a clear point of view or perspective orally when discussing texts.
- written_production: Write texts that show a clear point of view or unique perspective based on author, audience, and context.
- procedural_application: Apply knowledge of author, audience, and context to interpret and create texts with a clear perspective.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how author, audience, and context influence the point of view or perspective in a text.
- comprehension_response: Interpret texts by identifying the author's purpose and perspective based on context and audience.
Codes: 1.P.ST.2.b

Standard: 1.T.T.1
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Writing
Cognitive demand: DOK2_skills_concepts
Competency: Identify and use narrative techniques such as characters, setting, plot, and dialogue to understand and create stories.
Skills:
- Identify techniques used to craft stories, including characters, setting, major events, and dialogue.
- Identify a simple plot with a problem and solution.
- Describe traits of the main characters and explain how their words and actions support the central message, lesson, or moral of the story.
- With adult support, compare and contrast characters and their experiences in stories across diverse cultures.
- Use knowledge of narrative techniques to create texts that share real or imagined experiences and events with a sense of closure.
Observable behaviors:
- Identify characters, setting, major events, and dialogue in stories.
- Recognize a simple plot with a problem and solution.
- Describe main characters' traits and explain how their words and actions support the story's central message or moral.
- Compare and contrast characters and their experiences in stories from different cultures with adult support.
- Use knowledge of narrative techniques to create stories that share real or imagined experiences and have a clear ending.
Pedagogy terms: characters, setting, plot, problem and solution, dialogue, central message, lesson, moral, compare and contrast, narrative techniques, story creation, closure
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify narrative techniques such as characters, setting, plot, and dialogue in stories.
- written_production: Create texts using narrative techniques to share experiences and events with a sense of closure.
- procedural_application: Use knowledge of narrative techniques to create stories with real or imagined experiences and a clear ending.
- investigation_handson: Compare and contrast characters and their experiences in stories across diverse cultures with adult support.
- reasoning_explanation: Describe traits of main characters and explain how their words and actions support the central message, lesson, or moral of the story.
- comprehension_response: Identify a simple plot with a problem and solution.
Codes: 1.T.T.1
candidates.label: Narrative Techniques

candidates.text:
Standard: 1.P.ST.1
Domain primary: Comprehension
Domain secondary: Speaking & Listening
Cognitive demand: DOK3_strategic_thinking
Competency: Use knowledge of important context elements like background information, location, culture, time period, and current events to understand and create texts.
Skills:
- Use prior knowledge, research, and discussions to identify key context components.
- Consider how context impacts the purposes of the author and the audience.
- Explore how context shapes the author's decisions and the audience's responses during text interpretation and construction.
Observable behaviors:
- Identify key context components such as background information, geographic location, cultural influences, time period, and contemporary events when reading or discussing texts.
- Explain how context affects the author's purpose and the audience's understanding.
- Discuss how context influences the author's choices and the audience's reactions during reading and writing.
Pedagogy terms: context, author's purpose, audience, interpretation, construction, background knowledge
Required student actions:
- recognition_identification: Identify key components of context relevant to a text.
- oral_production: Discuss how context affects author and audience purposes and responses.
- procedural_application: Apply knowledge of context to interpret and construct texts.
- investigation_handson: Use prior knowledge, research, and discussions to gather context information.
- reasoning_explanation: Explain how context shapes author decisions and audience responses.
- comprehension_response: Interpret texts using understanding of context components.
Codes: 1.P.ST.1
candidates.label: Context
